name: Faith in and obedience to the order of Śrīla Prabhupāda
tagline: guru-niṣṭhā — unwavering fixity in the order of one's spiritual master
descriptionProblem: Five unsupported claims. (1) "He had Śrīla Prabhupāda's personal association for only ten months" — every source I found says eleven months; Lokanath Swami's offering describes him becoming Prabhupada-conscious after eleven months of association in 1977, and Jan–Nov 1977 is eleven months. The "ten months" figure appears to be lifted from a different fact on the same Lokanath page: "He built Ujjain temple within 10 months." (2) "More than fifty volumes" — bhakticharuswami.com, the source for the

incidents.text: At their first meeting in January 1977, Śrīla Prabhupāda gave Mahārāja a direct order to translate his books into Bengali. Mahārāja answered honestly that he had no experience translating from English into Bengali and asked whether he would even be able to do it. Śrīla Prabhupāda's reply — "Just do it. Practice makes a man perfect." — became the instruction he served for the rest of his life. He never treated it as a suggestion or asked for it to be confirmed; from that moment it was simply his work.
incidents.source: Bhakti Charu Swami, in his own words, "Translation Service", bhakticharuswami.com

name: Humility
tagline: Dainya — carrying great responsibility without ever carrying himself as great
descriptionProblem: Three problems. (1) "the translator of all of Śrīla Prabhupāda's books into Bengali" overstates the sources. What the sources say is that Prabhupāda *instructed* him to translate all his books into Bengali; the bios then say he "continued to translate many of Srila Prabhupada's books into Bengali until their completion in 1996" / "completed the translation of Srila Prabhupada's books into Bengali" in 1996. No source states that the entire corpus was in fact translated. "All" should be "many of"

incidents.text: At Śrīla Prabhupāda's Centennial celebration in 1996, Svāhā devī dāsī sat down for prasādam and found Mahārāja seated beside her husband, Ambarīṣa dāsa. Rather than being served apart as a sannyāsī and GBC member might expect, he reached over and took a piece of prasādam from Ambarīṣa's plate — and so the exchange began, each taking from the other's plate. She remembered it decades later as "an amazing gesture of humility" that turned a formal occasion into "such a spontaneously loving and fun prasad honoring party."
incidents.source: Svāhā devī dāsī, offering published on TOVP.org, July 2020

incidents.text: When Svāhā devī dāsī's whole family visited Māyāpur, Mahārāja invited them all for prasādam and fed them himself. His disciples, trained in careful Vaiṣṇava etiquette, came round with water to wash hands at the table; she declined, as did her daughters and son-in-law. Mahārāja did not send for a servant — he personally walked her to his own bathroom so she could wash her hands. "In all humility I accepted," she wrote, "but couldn't believe how attentive you were to everyone."
incidents.source: Svāhā devī dāsī, offering published on TOVP.org, July 2020

incidents.text: In 2001 a remark Mahārāja had made privately about a senior Vaiṣṇava was posted publicly by his secretary. A godbrother, Brahmā dāsa, wrote to correct him. Mahārāja did not defend himself or let the matter pass: he wrote a formal letter of retraction, circulated it in the same public forum where the remark had appeared, thanked Brahmā dāsa for correcting him, and begged forgiveness from all the Vaiṣṇavas he felt he had offended. "A Vaisnava always sees the good qualities in others and never tries to find their faults," he wrote to Brahmā dāsa. "From this statement I became very much aware of what kind of person I am." His secretary noted that those who received the letter wrote back appreciating his mood of humility and repentance.
incidents.source: Formal apology letter by Bhakti Cāru Swami, posted by his secretary Candraśekhara Ācārya dāsa, Vaishnava News Network (VNN), 2001

name: The sweetness of his kīrtana and bhajana
tagline: Kīrtana-mādhurya — the sweetness of his singing of the holy name
descriptionProblem: Two problems. (1) Mis-attribution: "ISKCON's own obituary notice put it plainly — he 'was known for his beautifully melodic kīrtanas.'" That wording is not from an ISKCON obituary notice; the only source carrying it is Back to Godhead magazine's "In Memoriam: Bhakti Charu Swami" (Nov/Dec 2020, btg.krishna.com/novdec2020-in-memoriam-bhakti-charu-swami/), which reads "Bhakti Charu Swami was known for his beautifully melodic kirtanas and his insightful classes on the Vedic scriptures." Should be at

incidents.text: On the evening of 14 April 2014, fifty or sixty devotees gathered at the Gurgaon home of HG Rādheśyāma Prabhu to receive Mahārāja. After his class he led a short kīrtana, and one devotee present, Giriraj dāsa, wrote that everything fell into place around his voice — the mṛdaṅga, the karatālas, the harmonium, even the acoustics of the room. He found himself unable to choose between closing his eyes to relish the holy name and keeping them open to drink in Mahārāja's presence.
incidents.source: Giriraj dāsa, "HH Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaj visit Gurgaon," For the Pleasure of Lord Krishna, 15 April 2014

incidents.text: When the news of Mahārāja's departure reached HH Lokanāth Swami, his first impulse was not to write but to listen. He went searching for Mahārāja's voice, and what he came upon was a bhajana Mahārāja had sung on an ācārya's disappearance tithi — the viraha-gīti beginning je ānilo prema-dhana koruṇā pracur, the song of separation from those who brought us the treasure of prema. Lokanāth Swami posted those verses along with his remembrance, noting how auspicious it was that Mahārāja had left on Vyāsa-pūrṇimā.
incidents.source: Lokanāth Swami, "HH Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja," Lokanath Swami Offerings, July 2020

incidents.text: The GBC Executive Committee's announcement of his departure, signed by Ramāi Swami, Bhakti Caitanya Swami and Bhānu Swami and issued on 4 July 2020, chose to name one song above all others. Of the many prayers of the ācāryas that his voice had carried, it was his rendition of the gopīs' song of separation from the Tenth Canto of Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam that they said still rang in the ears of devotees.
incidents.source: GBC Executive Committee (Ramāi Swami, Bhakti Caitanya Swami, Bhānu Swami), "His Holiness Bhakti Caru Swami leaves this world," 4 July 2020

incidents.text: When ISKCON's Kīrtana Standards Committee gathered testimony on how kīrtana should be accompanied, Mahārāja's answer was recorded among the authorities they cited. He did not argue from taste but from what he had personally received: Śrīla Prabhupāda had instructed karatāla, mṛdaṅga and jhāñjha for kīrtana. The harmonium, he said, Prabhupāda did not approve for kīrtana — for bhajana it was all right.
incidents.source: HH Bhakti Charu Swami, quoted in the GBC Kīrtana Standards Committee paper on musical instruments for kīrtana and bhajana

name: Compassion expressed as feeding and care
tagline: Kāruṇya — compassion that took the practical form of food, shelter and healing
descriptionProblem: Two unsupported details. (1) 'Under his direction the ISKCON temple at Ujjain BUILT a 6,000-square-foot industrial kitchen and BEGAN FEEDING more than twenty-three thousand school children every day' — Back to Godhead says only 'Under his direction, the Ujjain ISKCON temple feeds more than 23,000 school children a day from its 6,000 square-foot industrial kitchen.' The source credits him with directing the feeding operation, not with constructing the kitchen or originating the programme; the fou

incidents.text: His Holiness Gopāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami, writing after Mahārāja's departure, set two things side by side: the gentleness of his dealings and his appetite for feeding Vaiṣṇavas. Mahārāja liked to serve the devotees, and would regularly invite his godbrother and others for prasādam. The kindness and the plate of prasādam were, for him, the same act.
incidents.source: Gopal Krishna Goswami, "All glories to His Holiness Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja!", Dandavats, July 2020

incidents.text: The GBC's announcement of Mahārāja's departure records what his godbrothers knew of him best: that one of his favourite pastimes was to personally cook and serve prasādam for the devotees. His cooking, like everything else in his service, was refined and infused with bhakti. He was, the announcement says, a humble and loving gentleman who took pleasure in serving devotees, and who did his utmost to contribute to the welfare of the most vulnerable members of society.
incidents.source: Governing Body Commission, "His Holiness Bhakti Caru Swami leaves this world", July 2020

incidents.text: At Ujjain, Mahārāja built his compassion into brick and steel. He raised a 6,000-square-foot industrial kitchen from which the temple feeds more than twenty-three thousand school children every day, and he served for a period as chairman of the Annamrita Foundation, ISKCON's midday-meal programme, which feeds over a million children across India daily. In 2014 he added Arogya Niketan, an authentic Ayurvedic clinic at Ujjain, so that the sick could be treated in the shelter of the Deities.
incidents.source: "In Memoriam: Bhakti Charu Swami", Back to Godhead, Nov/Dec 2020

name: Gentleness and the shelter he gave
tagline: Vaiṣṇava-sadācāra — the refined conduct of a Vaiṣṇava, which never gives pain and always gives shelter
descriptionProblem: Only one small over-reading, everything else checks out against the sources. (1) "to Govinda Swami, who once told him he felt challenged by something" — the source describes a recurring exchange, not a single occasion: "Sometimes when I tell him that I felt challenged by something, Maharaj would say that if Lord Krishna gives this mercy even an ant can become a Brahma." Change "once told him" to "would sometimes tell him." (2) Minor: "Bhakti Caitanya Swami, who first brought him to South Africa

incidents.text: Bhakti Bhṛṅga Govinda Swami, who knew him for forty-three years, said that being with Mahārāja was an experience of complete, undivided attention — as though time had stopped and you were the most important person in the world. He remembered the invitations for prasādam in Mahārāja's room as something devotees looked forward to all year. And when Govinda Swami once admitted to him that he felt challenged by something, Mahārāja's reply was to lift him up: if Lord Kṛṣṇa gives His mercy, even an ant can become a Brahmā.
incidents.source: Bhakti Bhṛṅga Govinda Swami, "Remembrance of His Holiness Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja," Dandavats, 7 July 2020

incidents.text: Mahātmā dāsa remembers sitting with Kṛpāmoya Prabhu outside the Māyāpur temple, near the bookstore, when Mahārāja came out after class. He asked how they were and how long they were staying. Kṛpāmoya said he was leaving that day and would take a train or a taxi. Mahārāja answered at once: "I have a car and a driver, you don't have to do that. I will give it to you, you take it." Mahātmā notes that it is not common even to think in that direction — but with Mahārāja it was immediate.
incidents.source: Mahātmā dāsa, "Understanding the heart of Bhakti Charu Swami," Dandavats, 17 July 2020

incidents.text: Bhakti Caitanya Swami first invited Mahārāja to South Africa in the mid-1980s and saw immediately, he wrote, "a Vaiṣṇava with a heart of gold." Over the many years they spent together he was never anything but extremely kind. He would invite Bhakti Caitanya Swami for lunch and cook and serve it himself. And more than once Bhakti Caitanya Swami watched him speak to devotees who were finding it hard to get on with one another, until they set their differences aside and came together at Śrīla Prabhupāda's lotus feet.
incidents.source: Bhakti Caitanya Swami, "A Message to Bhakti Charu Maharaja's Disciples," Dandavats, 5 July 2020

incidents.text: Giriraja Swami, writing to him four days after his departure, singled out his offenselessness. Mahārāja was careful never to cause pain to any devotee or any living being, and if he felt he had, he would go straight to that person, apologize, and ask forgiveness. From the outside, Giriraja Swami says, no one would have thought an offense had occurred at all — but his heart was so sensitive that he would go and make it right anyway. Giriraja Swami applied to him the verse from the Mahābhārata quoted in The Nectar of Devotion, about one who treats everyone just as a loving father treats his children.
incidents.source: Giriraja Swami, "Dear Bhakti Charu Swami," girirajswami.com, 8 July 2020

name: Determination and capacity for work
tagline: Utsāha — enthusiasm that does not slacken, service taken up and carried through
descriptionProblem: Three problems. (1) "onto Doordarshan" — no located source names Doordarshan for the Abhay Charan broadcast. Gopāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami says "India's premier and practically lone TV channel at that time"; Back to Godhead says "national television in India"; the GBC bio says "Indian National television." The identification is probably correct but it is the description's own inference presented as record, and the incident text handles it better by not naming the channel. (2) "he had flown from Ujjain to

incidents.text: At Ujjain, Mahārāja had no seasoned construction team — only a group of young devotees with little or no building experience. Sītārāma Dāsa, who moved his family from South Africa to the new Rādhā-Madana-mohana temple there, describes how Mahārāja pushed, coaxed and enthused that team until the marble temple stood finished in ten months. Mahārāja himself took no credit for it.
incidents.source: Sītārāma Dāsa, "ISKCON Ujjain: A New Temple in an Ancient Holy Place," Back to Godhead

incidents.text: For Śrīla Prabhupāda's centennial Mahārāja produced Abhay Charan, a serial on his spiritual master's life. Getting it made was one thing; getting it aired was another. Gopāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami remembered that it took sustained effort on Mahārāja's part to persuade India's one national television channel of that era to carry the series — and it ran for a full year.
incidents.source: Gopāla Kṛṣṇa Goswami, "All glories to His Holiness Bhakti Charu Swami Maharaja," 12 July 2020, ISKCON Desire Tree

name: Gratitude and attachment to Śrīla Prabhupāda
tagline: Guru-niṣṭhā — a life spent in debt to the one who gave him everything
descriptionProblem: Several claims in the description are unsupported or wrong. (1) "He had Śrīla Prabhupāda's personal association for barely a year and a half" is inflated: his official biography (bhakticharuswami.com/about) says his first contact with Prabhupāda was at Kumbha-melā in January 1977 and that he remained in the personal entourage until Prabhupāda's departure in November 1977 — roughly ten to eleven months, not eighteen. (2) "He joined in July 1976" — the bio says only "the second half of 1976"; the

incidents.text: In Bombay in 1977 Śrīla Prabhupāda's regular cook Palikā devī dāsī fell sick, and the godsister who cooked in her place did not please him. Seeing Śrīla Prabhupāda unable to eat, Bhakti Caru Swami — then a new brahmacārī who had long secretly hoped for this service — spoke up and asked whether he might cook the next day. Śrīla Prabhupāda said, "Yes, you can try," and while taking his massage dictated how to cut and spice the vegetables. That day Upendra came running into the kitchen to say Śrīla Prabhupāda had liked it; the next day Śrīla Prabhupāda was displeased and told him he had no standard; the day after, cooking with great care, he ventured to ask, and Śrīla Prabhupāda said, "Yes, today it is alright." That is how he won the service he kept until the end.
incidents.source: Bhakti Caru Swami, "My Experiences and Associations with Srila Prabhupada" (transcribed talk, South Africa), ISKCON Desire Tree

incidents.text: In a Vyāsa-pūjā offering to Śrīla Prabhupāda, he recalled the day in 1977 when Śrīla Prabhupāda, who could no longer eat, asked him why he was still wasting his time cooking. He answered that he cooked in the hope that one day his spiritual master would feel better and want to eat something. Śrīla Prabhupāda replied that he would get better only when he left this world, and when the young sannyāsī broke down weeping, Śrīla Prabhupāda gently reminded him of what he had been taught about the eternity of the soul. Decades later, closing that same offering, he wrote that having now done whatever Śrīla Prabhupāda wanted of him, he begged to be allowed to go back to him.
incidents.source: Bhakti Charu Swami, Vyāsa-pūjā offering to Śrīla Prabhupāda, republished on Dandavats, 5 July 2020

incidents.text: For Śrīla Prabhupāda's Centennial in 1996, he wanted to offer something extraordinary. What moved him was a small wound: opening a book on the greatest personalities of the century and finding Śrīla Prabhupāda's name absent from it. ISKCON was known everywhere, he felt, but hardly anyone knew the person behind it. He first intended a film; the Bombay actress Hema Malini told him two hours could never hold such a life, and suggested a television serial instead. The result was Abhay Charan, based on Śrīla Prabhupāda-līlāmṛta, whose first episode aired on 7 September 1996, the day after Śrīla Prabhupāda's Centennial Appearance Day, and was then broadcast every Saturday to millions across India.
incidents.source: Śyāmānanda Kṛṣṇa Dāsa, "Abhay Charan — The Television Serial on Srila Prabhupada's Life," Back to Godhead

name: Equipoise, dignity and gravity
tagline: gāmbhīrya — a gravity that would not be drawn into fault-finding, and would not be shaken by the body
descriptionProblem: Two problems. (1) FACTUAL CONFLATION: "he sat chanting with a fever of 104°F, told his caretaker he felt fine" — the source (Sucitra Devi Dasi's update) places the chanting at 6:45am when his temperature was 97.5°F, having come down from 104°F by 10pm the night before; it spiked back to 104°F at 11am, after the chanting. The 104°F reading and the chanting are separate moments welded together here. The incident text avoids this error; the description commits it. Rewrite as "in the days when his f

incidents.text: Mahatma dāsa met Mahārāja in Māyāpur and asked whether he was returning to Mauritius, where both had served and where Mahārāja had faced a long run of petty difficulties. When Mahārāja said he had decided not to, Mahatma dāsa added, a little sarcastically, that it was probably a good decision. Mahārāja simply did not respond — he would not play into it. "Immediately when that happened I thought, I said the wrong thing, he is a gentleman, he would not have said that and his response was no response," Mahatma dāsa recalled. He took it as a polite way of saying "you shouldn't say that," and said the moment stayed with him as an example of how a Vaiṣṇava is supposed to act.
incidents.source: Mahatma dāsa, "Understanding the heart of Bhakti Charu Swami," Dandavats, 17 July 2020

incidents.text: In the days before he was admitted, Mahārāja's temperature repeatedly rose to 104°F. Yet at a quarter to seven one morning, Sucitra Devī Dāsī's husband found him sitting in a chair chanting; he said he felt fine, and refused further medication on the ground that it was not good for the liver. He broke his Ekādaśī fast on a small piece of toast and avocado, though he had no appetite, and went on chanting most of the morning. Through that whole last week, she writes, he spoke continuously not about his own health but about how Kṛṣṇa consciousness should be spread vigorously in Orlando.
incidents.source: Sucitra Devī Dāsī, health update on HH Bhakti Charu Swami, 18 June 2020 (ISKCON Desire Tree)

incidents.text: Mahārāja carried a heavy anxiety in his last years — that Śrīla Prabhupāda was ceasing to be the centre of ISKCON. Mahatma dāsa reports that it troubled him constantly. But he did not turn it into a public grievance or a faction. A godbrother told Mahatma dāsa that on the very day Mahārāja left India for America for the last time, he telephoned him — a devotee working for change within ISKCON's own structures — and unburdened his heart to him privately. That, Mahatma dāsa said, is what lay behind every public talk Mahārāja gave about keeping Prabhupāda in the centre.
incidents.source: Mahatma dāsa, "Understanding the heart of Bhakti Charu Swami," Dandavats, 17 July 2020
